title: Hodgkin lymphoma
subtitle: Highly curable, and managed by interim PET more than by anything else — the whole game is giving enough therapy to cure while withdrawing bleomycin and radiation from the people who don't need them
source: Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Hodgkin, pp.181–192 (Chou L, Schroers-Martin J) · NCCN v2.2025 · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter

blocks.heading: Workup
items: History: B symptoms, pruritus, alcohol intolerance; exam of nodal regions, liver, spleen. Marrow biopsy only for focal bone lesions or unexplained cytopenias
IHC — most critical: CD30, CD15, PAX5, CD20, CD3
Labs: CBC, CMP, ESR, LDH, HIV, hepatitis B and C
Echo/MUGA before anthracycline · PFTs before bleomycin · before a checkpoint inhibitor: TSH, ACTH, cortisol, troponin
Fertility discussion — risk is low with A(B)VD, so preservation is not mandated frontline; bank before salvage

blocks.heading: Staging — Cotswolds-modified Ann Arbor
rows: One lymph node region or lymphoid structure (spleen, thymus, Waldeyer ring)
≥2 regions, same side of the diaphragm. Hilar nodes are lateralized — bilateral involvement is stage II
Regions on both sides of the diaphragm
Disseminated — marrow, CNS, or more than one extranodal site
B = weight loss >10% over 6 mo, or unexplained fever >38°C in the past month, or recurrent drenching night sweats
S splenic · X bulky: node ≥10 cm, or mediastinal mass ≥⅓ the transverse thoracic diameter at T5–6 · E limited direct extranodal extension
blocks.footnote: A single extranodal site as the only disease is IE; more than one extranodal site is stage IV. Hilar (bronchopulmonary) nodes sit outside the mediastinum.

blocks.heading: Early-stage risk factors
blocks.footnote: Favorable = CS I–II with none of these. GHSG counts nodal areas differently from Ann Arbor (infraclavicular with ipsilateral cervical, both hila with mediastinum, abdomen split in two).

blocks.heading: IPS — advanced stage
blocks.footnote: One point each: albumin <4 · Hgb <10.5 · male · stage IV · age ≥45 · WBC ≥15,000 · lymphocytes <600 or <8%. Hasenclever NEJM 1998; Moccia JCO 2012 is the modern-era revision.

chains.header: Early favorable (CS I–II, no risk factors)

boxes: Checkpoint combo is preferred first salvage
non-CPI: BeGEV, BV ± benda, BV-ICE, DHAP, GVD, ICE
transformation to THRLBCL → treat as DLBCL

blocks.heading: † Deauville 5-point score
rows: Uptake > mediastinum but ≤ liver — usually adequate response
Moderately > liver · markedly > liver or new lesions — treatment failure
blocks.footnote: † Not in the handbook chapter, which specifies only PET/CT at completion (plus marrow biopsy if positive at diagnosis). Added because response is reported this way in practice and in every trial cited here.

blocks.heading: Frontline regimens
rows: Doxorubicin 25 · bleomycin 10 units/m² · vinblastine 6 · dacarbazine 375 — all d1 + d15
Nivolumab 240 mg · doxorubicin 25 · vinblastine 6 · dacarbazine 375 — all d1 + d15. G-CSF not required
Brentuximab 1.8 d0 · etoposide 150 d1–3 · cyclophosphamide 1250 d1 · doxorubicin 40 d1 · vincristine 1.4 d8 · dacarbazine 250 d2–3 · dexamethasone 40 mg d1–4
Brentuximab 1.2 mg/kg · doxorubicin 25 · vinblastine 6 · dacarbazine 375 — all d1 + d15; filgrastim d5–8 and d19–22
blocks.footnote: mg/m² unless stated. BrECADD starts at dose level 4 and de-escalates for toxicity. Antiviral + PJP prophylaxis with every brentuximab-containing regimen.

blocks.heading: Salvage regimens
rows: Pembrolizumab 200 mg d1; gemcitabine 1000 (800 if post-HSCT) + vinorelbine 15 + liposomal doxorubicin 10 — all d1 + d8
Checkpoint inhibitor d1 + ICE: ifosfamide 5000 + mesna 5000 CIV d2; carboplatin AUC 5 (max 800 mg) d2; etoposide 100 d1–3
Brentuximab 1.8 mg/kg (max 180 mg) d1; nivolumab 240 mg C1D8 then d1 of C2–4
Brentuximab 1.8 mg/kg d1 ± bendamustine 90 d1–2 (BV alone ×16 cycles) · BeGEV = gemcitabine 800 d1+4, bendamustine 90 d2+3, vinorelbine 20 d1, prednisolone 100 mg d1–4
Gemcitabine/vinorelbine/liposomal doxorubicin · ifosfamide-carbo-etoposide · cisplatin + cytarabine 2000 q12h ×2 + dexamethasone
blocks.footnote: 2–4 cycles then mobilization for transplant candidates, 4–6 otherwise. Checkpoint monotherapy responds often but completes rarely — combine it.

blocks.heading: Pearls
items: Do not give G-CSF with ABVD — bleomycin pulmonary toxicity. Do not delay or dose-reduce for non-febrile neutropenia; if unavoidable (ANC <200 or febrile neutropenia) give it day 5 or later ×3–5 days
Bilateral hilar involvement is stage II, not III — hilar nodes are lateralized, and they sit outside the mediastinum
In relapse, give a checkpoint combination first if the patient is CPI-naive — post-ASCT outcomes are better
† The handbook defers survivorship to NCCN — cardiac late effects, second malignancy and post-chest-RT breast screening are not in it

blocks.heading: Trials behind the pathway
rows: ABVD ×2 + 20 Gy for GHSG-favorable early stage with a negative interim PET
PET-adapted radiation omission vs combined modality in early stage
Drop bleomycin after 2 cycles if interim PET is negative
BrECADD vs eBEACOPP in advanced stage — the current European standard
blocks.footnote: HD16, RAPID and H10 all failed non-inferiority — omitting RT costs ~4–7% PFS, though OS is unchanged.

Hilar nodes are lateralized — bilateral involvement is stage II III Regions on both sides of the diaphragm IV Disseminated — marrow, CNS, or more than one extranodal site A / B B = weight loss >10% over 6 mo, or unexplained fever >38°C in the past month, or recurrent drenching night sweats S · X · E S splenic · X bulky: node ≥10 cm , or mediastinal mass ≥⅓ the transverse thoracic diameter at T5–6 · E limited direct extranodal extension A single extranodal site as the only disease is IE; more than one extranodal site is stage IV. Hilar (bronchopulmonary) nodes sit outside the mediastinum. Early-stage risk factors Factor EORTC GHSG NCCN Mediastinal mass >0.35 CXR >⅓ CXR >⅓ or >10 cm Age ≥50 yes — — ESR ≥50 (≥30 if B) ≥50 (≥30 if B) ≥50 or any B Extranodal disease — yes — Nodal areas ≥3 ≥2 ≥3 Favorable = CS I–II with none of these. GHSG counts nodal areas differently from Ann Arbor (infraclavicular with ipsilateral cervical, both hila with mediastinum, abdomen split in two). IPS — advanced stage Factors FFP Hasenclever FFP Moccia 0–1 84–77% 88–84% 2–3 67–60% 80–74% ≥4 51–42% 67–62% One point each: albumin <4 · Hgb <10.5 · male · stage IV · age ≥45 · WBC ≥15,000 · lymphocytes <600 or <8% . Hasenclever NEJM 1998; Moccia JCO 2012 is the modern-era revision. Treatment pathway Early favorable (CS I–II, no risk factors) PET-adapted, two routes GHSG-favorable: ABVD ×2 → 20 Gy ISRT (HD16) otherwise ABVD ×3 → 30 Gy if DS 1–2 chemo only: ABVD ×4 if DS 1–2 DS 3 → ABVD ×2 then AVD ×4 (RATHL) Early unfavorable Combined modality or chemo alone ABVD ×4 + 30 Gy ISRT if DS 1–2 nivo-AVD ×4 + 30 Gy (NIVAHL) · BV-AVD (BREACH) chemo only: ABVD ×2 → AVD ×4 — drop bleomycin after cycle 2 if DS 1–3 (RATHL) Advanced III–IV Two modern standards BrECADD ×4–6 (HD21) — stop at 4 if DS 1–3 nivolumab-AVD ×6 (S1826) selected: BV-AVD ×6 (ECHELON-1), ABVD Relapsed / refractory Checkpoint combo is preferred first salvage pembro-GVD · pembro-ICE · nivo-ICE · BV-nivo non-CPI: BeGEV, BV ± benda, BV-ICE, DHAP, GVD, ICE 2–4 cycles then mobilize if transplant-bound NLPHL A different disease I–IIA contiguous non-bulky: ISRT 30–36 Gy I–IIB or bulky: R-ABVD/R-CHOP ×4 + 30 Gy III–IV: R-CHOP ×6 ± ISRT, or observe transformation to THRLBCL → treat as DLBCL † Deauville 5-point score 1 · 2 No uptake · uptake ≤ mediastinum 3 Uptake > mediastinum but ≤ liver — usually adequate response 4 · 5 Moderately > liver · markedly > liver or new lesions — treatment failure † Not in the handbook chapter, which specifies only PET/CT at completion (plus marrow biopsy if positive at diagnosis).
